recipes.name: Haluski - Cabbage and Noodles
ingredients_raw: 2 small heads cabbage, cored and cut into 1-inch pieces
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 300 degrees F (150 degrees C).
Fill a large pot with lightly salted water and bring to a rolling boil. Stir in egg noodles and return to a boil.
Cook noodles uncovered, stirring occasionally, until tender yet firm to the bite, about 5 minutes. Drain well and set aside.
Melt 1/2 cup butter in a large skillet over medium-low heat. Add onions; cook and stir in hot butter until translucent, 5 to 10 minutes.
Add cabbage and remaining 1/2 cup butter to onions in the skillet; cook and stir until cabbage is softened but not browned, 5 to 8 minutes. Season with salt and black pepper.
Place cooked noodles and cabbage mixture in a large roasting pan; stir gently to combine. Sprinkle with more salt and black pepper, if desired.
Bake in the preheated oven until the top is golden brown, 30 to 40 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Haluski - Cabbage and Noodles
raw_recipe.description: This haluski recipe is a quick and simple comforting side dish of buttery fried cabbage and onions with noodles, baked and ready in less than 1 hour.

video.description: Egg noodles, cooked cabbage, and onions makes a delicious dinner!

review.reviewBody:
We love Haluski, altought I've never made it from "scratch" before. I've always bought it pre-made, frozen. So this was a first, this is a perfect base recipe but we like a little more flavor.
MY TIP: Add a meat, like bacon or kielbaska- brown the meat first, set meat aside, then add the butter, onions...and so forth, into the meat drippings. Follow the recipe from there. Lastly chop up the meat into tiny pieces and add to the noodles. Also, a little sprinkling of garlic powder adds another flavor layer. Consider adding a box of frozen pierogi's at the very end and cook app 10 minutes longer till hot in the center. Still very simple and very good.

Why bake this? I make the noodles, cook a whole cut-up cabbage and onions with a stick of butter, then mix them together when the cabbage is tender and add another stick of butter with salt and pepper. The baking part doesn't make any sense to me. I'm Hungarian! Other than that this is one of my favorite recipes. Sometimes I add caraway seeds. This also makes great leftovers as it's easy to reheat in the microwave.

I ALWAYS ALWAYS ADD BACON! But I also add fresh garlic and sauteed fresh mushrooms. I double the onions as well and I caramelize them first. I'm sure that purists would say that all that this can no longer be able to be called "Haluski," but I just call it delectable. In this form, it becomes a meal.

I'm a lover of Cabbage and Buttered Noodles HOWEVER: I'm A LAZY HAPPY COOK: INTO THE MICROWAVE GOES A SMALL BOWL OF: LOTS OF CUT UP ONIONS & GARLIC WITH SOME EXTRA VIRGIN OLIVE OIL, & SMALLER AMT OF BUTTER (cover with lid or a paper towel - 2 minutes) then cook up your chopped up cabbage in a bit of water & olive oil....start wmedium heat and lower to simmer......leave it (with stirring it while waiting) - just when it's getting soft enough....start to boil your noodles (or potato dumplings) - then mix together with your hot cabbage, onions, garlic, salt, pepper and ENJOY! PS: Sometimes I like adding some Navy Beans for more taste and protein!

The basics of this recipe are very good, however, I did do some adjustments to it. I never put mine in the oven. I chop up a whole big head of cabbage and add that to my caramelized onions that I've cooked in bacon grease. I wilt down the cabbage with the cooked onions for a little bit and then I add in some chicken stock. I cover the whole thing with a lid or some foil and let it simmer for about two and a half hours. I do add in either some cottage cheese or sour cream for taste. I tend to add in quite a bit of pepper as well. It ends up being so delicious served with either klusky noodles or wide egg noodles. I also add in about six strips of applewood bacon crumbled.

Fried bacon and cooked everything in some of the fat and butter. Also added some caraway seeds with the cabbage and finished with sour cream. Crumble the bacon on top. No Ned to bake! Delicious right out of the pan!

This is a delicious side dish. I do not bake this, but I fried about 4 strips of cut up raw bacon pieces (1/2 inch size) and also two cups of cut up smoked polish sausage (kielbasa) along with the onion before adding other ingredients and it makes just a fabulous side dish that we will have with BBQ ribs. and a cucumber salad. What a great meal! This is one of my hubby's favorites.
I love making Haluski, but I find it much easier to simply complete it stove top. I've not heard of baking or finishing in the oven. No extra dirty dishes for me;)

I used cut up bacon, used that bacon grease and added butter then the onions. Sooooo good! Also added some cajun seasoning. I've made this 3 times now. Shared it with my aunt and she's made it a few times now, switching up the flavors. Really great jumping off point recipe!

I decided to make this recipe because I love cabbage. I tweaked it by adding fresh garlic cloves with the onion. Also added chopped rotisserie chicken for protein. I cooked the noodles in chicken broth and then use the broth to add into the pan when I put it in the oven to prevent it from drying out. This is a good stick to your ribs winter dish.

Love it! But here’s a twist that I learned from my husbands grandmother who’s was Slovak. Brown one stick of unsalted butter, turn down heat and add onions a cabbage, cover and simmer for about two hours. Add noodles and salt to taste! I do the same when making Perogies, changes the taste for the better!
No changes

It is a terribly simple recipe, but if you're in hurry (as I often am) I cook the noodles and cabbage just short of done, combine them, add the second half of the butter and finish it off on the stovetop. I never make it without bacon or sausage. I particularly like shopped kabanosy sausage for it. If you're not worried about calories, don't drain any fat from the bacon or sausage and just add it in. If you want to "Irish it up" minced corned beef works very well too.

I made it but didn't baked it. I cooked the noodles ahead of time and set to side after I sauté the onions I put the kielbasa into the pan to brown them can I edit my cabbage to it a little more butter a little water is steamed. It kept stirring until the cabbage broke down his size cooking. I turned it off and added my noodles to it. The heat from the cabbage finish cooking the noodles. I also added 1/2 of small red cabbage to offset the bitterness that you get for a regular cabbage.. family really loved it

So good as is. My grandma would sometimes fancy it up by making a roux (Butter, Flour, Milk, Salt & Pepper) to pour over it. You can always tell a good Polish recipe when it starts with "Cabbage, Onion, Butter..."
I halved this recipe and it BARELY fit in the largest pan I had. Was great with some added kilebasa and garlic.
Very good! I topped with extra onions I had cooked in bacon fat...because I love onions and I had sliced too many to start!🤷
I added sausage, it was outstanding.
This is a good recipe. I graded my homemade bread rolls on top of the casserole and sprinkled a little bit of cheese yummy.
Way to much butter. Loved it other than that.
